## ANTIBIOTIC PRESCRIBING PEARLS

## 1. Antibiotic stewardship

- Prevent antimicrobial overuse, misuse, and abuse.
- Minimize resistance.
- Reduce health care-associated costs.

## Beta-Lactam ring

- Beta-lactamase producing bugs
- Allergic reactions

## Antibiotic Stewardship

- The 5 Ds:
- $ Drug (right drug for the right bug)
- $ Dosing (optimal)
- $ Drug route
- $ Duration (suitable)
- $ De-escalation (timely to pathogen-directed therapy)

Susceptibility does not equal sensitivity due to resistance!

## Antibiotic Duration

<!-- image -->

## Most indications require 5 to 7 days of treatment

- Clinical improvement at 48 hours

## Longer courses required:

- Streptococcal pharyngitis (10 days)
- Pyelonephritis (14 days)
- Severe infections
- Immunocompromised patients
- Many pediatric indications

## Empiric Therapy

The first-line antibiotic that targets the most likely organisms

| Patient Considerations                                                                                                    | Antibiotic Resistance                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| · Risk of morbidity/mortality · Higher risk: choose a broader spectrum · Risk of side effects · Patient contraindications | antibiotic · Antibiogram "ESKAPE" (Enterococci, S. aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter spp.) |

## When Do We Get a Culture?

- Order a culture if:
- $ Patient cannot afford treatment failure!
- $ Severe infection
- $ Patient at risk for complications
- $ Unsure of organism or presence of infection
- $ Failed empiric treatment
- $ High risk of resistance (recent antibiotics)

Site/sample must be appropriate for culture!

## What Is a "Beta-Lactam" Antibiotic?

An antibiotic with a beta-lactam ring

<!-- image -->

## A patient says, "I'm allergic to penicillin."

Is it safe to prescribe a cephalosporin?

## What Are They Allergic to?

Patients who have penicillin allergy are allergic to either the pink pentagon or the blue box.

<!-- image -->

NOTES

## NOTES How Common Is Allergy to Both Penicillin and Cephalosporins?

- IgE-mediated cross-reactivity is very uncommon!
- Strongest possibility if similar R1 chemical side chain
- 1-8%: first/second generation cephalosporins
- <1%: third-generation cephalosporins

## Penicillin

## Cephalosporin

<!-- image -->

## PRESCRIBING RULES FOR PENICILLIN ALLERGY

## Rule 1: NEVER Give a First-Generation Cephalosporin if

The reaction to penicillin was anaphylaxis or hives!

Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated, type I hypersensitivity reaction: Each reaction progressively worsens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Other IgE-mediated symptoms: hypotension, laryngeal edema, wheezing, angioedema, or urticaria (hives)

## Rule 2: Cautious Use of Second- or Third-Generation Cephalosporin if

- Type 1 hypersensitivity to PCN
- Later generations have dissimilar chemical side chains. ➔ Less potential for cross-reactivity
- Less potential for cross-reactivity if >10 years since allergic reaction to penicillin

TIP: <1% of the population has a true PCN allergy.

## Rule 3: Give Any Cephalosporin if

- The reaction to penicillin was a morbilliform rash.
- Maculopapular drug eruption; usually T cell mediated (type IV hypersensitivity)

<!-- image -->

## QUESTION #1

Which of the following statements about morbilliform rash is true?

1. It is not considered an allergic reaction, but a drug-disease reaction.
2. The rash always appears within 24-48 hours after administration of the drug.
3. Penicillin and cephalosporins are commonly associated with morbilliform rash.
4. The rash associated with maculopapular drug eruption may extend to the mucous membranes.

## Hives vs. Morbilliform Rash HIVES

- Raised wheals
- Red on light skin, hypopigmented on dark skin
- Intensely itchy
- Appear suddenly and spreads quickly
- Escalates with each exposure
- Size and shape of lesions change frequently
- Type I hypersensitivity (IgE mediated)

## Note the Different Appearance

## Hives

<!-- image -->

## MORBILLIFORM RASH

- Maculopapular, coalescing rash on extremities and trunk (not mucus membranes)
- Mild itching/burning
- Common in children
- Antibiotics are a common cause (betalactams, quinolones, sulfas); infection may also be cause; NSAIDs; antiepileptic drugs
- Type IV hypersensitivity (T cell mediated)

## NOTES

## NOTES The second reason the beta-lactam ring is important:

Antibiotic resistance!

## Beta-Lactamase

Smart bacteria learned to produce beta-lactamase to destroy the beta-lactam ring.

<!-- image -->

## Fighting Beta-Lactamase

Beta-lactam ring shields against the beta-lactamase producers.

- Penicillin: Augmentin = amoxicillin/clavulanic acid
- Cephalosporins: third-generation cephalosporins

<!-- image -->

## THE ANTIBIOTICS

## Penicillin

|                                                                                                                                                            | Ampicillin, Amoxicillin Penicillin G, Penicillin K Gram-Positive Organisms   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Gram-Positive                                                                                                                                              | Gram-Positive                                                                |
| Streptococcus Group A, B, C, G Enterococcus Streptococcus pneumoniae Drug-resistant S. pneumoniae (DRSP) C. botulinum (wound, not food) NOT Staphylococcus |                                                                              |

Common indications: streptococcal pharyngitis, pneumonia, dental abscess, syphilis, AOM, sinusitis

## Extended-Spectrum Penicillin

| Amoxicillin/clavulanate (Augmentin) - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Atypical Organisms Beta-Lactamase Producers - Gram-Positive   | Amoxicillin/clavulanate (Augmentin) - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Atypical Organisms Beta-Lactamase Producers - Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Strep. Group A, B, C, G                                                                                                           | H. influenzae                                                                                                                              |
| Enterococcus                                                                                                                      | M. catarrhalis                                                                                                                             |
| Streptococcus pneumoniae                                                                                                          | E. coli                                                                                                                                    |
| DRSP                                                                                                                              | Neisseria                                                                                                                                  |
| MSSA                                                                                                                              | C. Diphtheria                                                                                                                              |
| NOT MRSA                                                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                            |

Common indications: sinusitis, AOM, streptococcal pharyngitis, bite wounds, pneumonia, diverticulitis

## QUESTION #2

A patient presents with recurrent bacterial sinusitis. Which risk factor increases the likelihood that the organism causing infection can produce betalactamase?

1. The patient presents with a fever.
2. The patient is immunocompromised.
3. The patient is older than age 65.
4. The patient was treated with amoxicillin last month.

## Cephalosporin Generations

| Generation   | Spectrum of Coverage                                                          |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| First        | Gram-positive, weak gram-negative                                             |
| Second       | Less gram-positive, more gram-negative                                        |
| Third        | Less gram-positive, extended gram-negative coverage, beta-lactamase producers |
| Fourth (IV)  | Gram-positive, stronger gram-negative, weak beta-lactamase                    |
| Fifth (V)    | Stronger gram-positive, gram-negative, beta-lactamase                         |

*4th/5th generation only available in intravenous formulation

## First-Generation Cephalosporins

| Cephalexin, Cefadroxil - Gram-Positive   | Cephalexin, Cefadroxil - Weak Gram-Negative Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Enterococcus                             | Proteus mirabilis                                                    |
| Streptococcus spp.                       | E. coli                                                              |
| Staphylococcus: MSSA                     | Klebsiella pneumoniae                                                |
| NOT MRSA                                 | (Special populations only)                                           |

Common indications: cellulitis, streptococcal pharyngitis, cystitis

<!-- image -->

## NOTES

## NOTES Second-Generation Cephalosporins

| Cefuroxime, Cefaclor, Cefprozil - Gram-Positive   | Cefuroxime, Cefaclor, Cefprozil - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Streptococcus                                     | H. influenzae (cefuroxime)                                                              |
| Staphylococcus: MSSA                              | E. coli                                                                                 |
| NOT MRSA                                          | Proteus mirabilis                                                                       |
|                                                   | Borrelia spp. (cefuroxime)                                                              |

Common indications: sinusitis, AOM

## Third-Generation Cephalosporins

| Ceftibuten, Cefixime                                                 | Ceftibuten, Cefixime                                                 |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Weak Gram-Positive, Stronger Gram-Negative, Beta-lactamase Producers | Weak Gram-Positive, Stronger Gram-Negative, Beta-lactamase Producers |
| Gram-Positive                                                        | Gram-Negative/Atypical                                               |
| Streptococcus groups                                                 | H. flu, M. cat,                                                      |
| NOT Staphylococcus                                                   | E. coli, Klebsiella                                                  |
|                                                                      | Salmonella, Shigella                                                 |

Common indications: rarely used unless positive C & S

## Third-Generation Extended-Spectrum Cephalosporins

| Ceftriaxone, Cefdinir, Cefpodoxime - Weak Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Gram-Positive   | Ceftriaxone, Cefdinir, Cefpodoxime - Beta-lactamase Producers Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Streptococcus groups                                                                    | H. flu, M. catarrhalis,                                                                |
| Staphylococcus: MSSA                                                                    | E. coli, Klebsiella                                                                    |
| NOT MRSA                                                                                | Proteus mirabilis                                                                      |
|                                                                                         | Gonorrhea (ceftriaxone)                                                                |

Common indications: gonorrhea, complicated/resistant AOM or sinusitis, pneumonia, pyelonephritis

## Sulfonamides

| Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) - Some Gram-Positive   | Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) - Broad Gram-Negative Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| MRSA (first-line)                                              | E. coli-(R)                                                                            |
| MSSA (not first-line)                                          | Klebsiella                                                                             |
| Streptococcus (R)                                              | Enterobacter                                                                           |
|                                                                | Shigella, Salmonella                                                                   |
|                                                                | Pneumocystis jirovecii                                                                 |

Common indications: cystitis, MRSA, PCP

## Tetracyclines

| Doxycycline, Tetracycline, Minocycline, Omadacycline, Sarecycline - Some Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Atypicals Gram-Positive   | Doxycycline, Tetracycline, Minocycline, Omadacycline, Sarecycline - Gram-Negative/Atypical                                                                            |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| MSSA MRSA: Doxycycline, Minocycline, Omadacycline Strep. (lower resp. tract): Doxycycline or Minocycline                         | Respiratory pathogens: H. flu, Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila Klebsiella Tick borne: Rickettsia, Borrelia E. coli-(R) Treponema-(R) Bacillus anthracis (Cutaneous anthrax) |

Common indications: Lyme disease, pneumonia, RMSF, MRSA, acne, chlamydia

## Macrolides

| Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, Erythromycin - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Gram-Positive   | Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, Erythromycin - Atypicals Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| MSSA                                                                                       | H. flu                                                                          |
| Streptococcus-R                                                                            | Gonorrhea/Chlamydia-R                                                           |
| Listeria                                                                                   | Bordetella pertussis                                                            |
| NOT MRSA                                                                                   | Salmonella                                                                      |
|                                                                                            | Legionella spp., Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila                                      |

Common indications: atypical pneumonia, pertussis, chlamydia (pregnancy)

## Fluoroquinolones

| Generation   | Spectrum of Coverage                                                                            |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Second       | Gram-negative (below the belt)                                                                  |
| Third        | Gram-positive, gram-negative Beta-lactamase producers, atypical pathogens, DRSP                 |
| Fourth       | Gram-positive, gram-negative (above the belt) Beta-lactamase producers atypical pathogens, DRSP |

## Second-Generation Fluoroquinolones

| Ciprofloxacin (Cipro), Ofloxacin (Floxin) - Gram-Negative, Atypicals - Gram-Positive   | Ciprofloxacin (Cipro), Ofloxacin (Floxin) - Gram-Negative, Atypicals - Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Staphylococcus: MSSA (eye and ear only)                                                | E. coli                                                                                         |
| Streptococcus - R                                                                      | Klebsiella                                                                                      |
| NOT Enterococcus                                                                       | Proteus spp.                                                                                    |
|                                                                                        | M. catarrhalis, H. flu,                                                                         |
|                                                                                        | Shigella                                                                                        |
|                                                                                        | Pseudomonas                                                                                     |

Common indications: conjunctivitis (ophthalmic), otitis externa (otic), pyelonephritis, cystitis, hot tub folliculitis, prostatitis

## NOTES

## NOTES Third-Generation Fluoroquinolones

| Levofloxacin (Levaquin) - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Atypical Pathogens, DRSP, aerobes, anaerobes Gram-Positive   | Levofloxacin (Levaquin) - Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Strep.: All types, DRSP!                                                                                             | E. coli, M. catarrhalis, H. flu,                   |
| Staph.: MSSA                                                                                                         | Klebsiella                                         |
| Listeria                                                                                                             | Legionella, Chlamydophila, Mycoplasma,             |
| NOT MRSA                                                                                                             | Pseudomonas (sometimes)                            |

Common indications: pneumonia, pyelonephritis, prostatitis

## Fourth-Generation Fluoroquinolones "Respiratory Fluoroquinolones"

| Moxifloxacin, Delafloxacin (Baxdela) - Gram-Positive, Gram-Negative, Gram-Positive   | Moxifloxacin, Delafloxacin (Baxdela) - Atypical Pathogens Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Streptococcus: All types, DRSP!                                                      | M. catarrhalis, H. flu                                                             |
| Staphylococcus: MSSA                                                                 | Chlamydia pneumoniae                                                               |
| Listeria                                                                             | Mycoplasma                                                                         |
| MRSA-only Delafloxacin                                                               | Legionella,                                                                        |
| Not urinary pathogens                                                                | E. coli, Klebsiella, Proteus (weak)                                                |

Common indications: pneumonia

## Nitrofuran

| Nitrofurantoin                                        | Nitrofurantoin                        |
|-------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Gram-Positive, Gram-Positive epidermidis Enterobacter | Pathogens Gram-Negative/Atypical coli |

Common indication: uncomplicated cystitis

## Lincosamide

| Clindamycin - Some Gram-Positive, Gram-Positive   | Clindamycin - Broad Gram-Negative Gram-Negative/Atypical   |
|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| Streptococcus: Pyogenes, pneumoniae               | Clostridium perfringens,                                   |
| Staphylococcus: MSSA and MRSA-CA                  | Toxoplasma gondii                                          |
|                                                   | Babesia spp. (Babesiosis)                                  |
|                                                   | Plasmodium spp. (Malaria)                                  |
|                                                   | Bacillus anthracis (Anthrax)                               |

Common indications: MRSA infections, bacterial vaginosis; Alternative for streptococcal pharyngitis, diverticulitis, AOM

High propensity to cause C. difficile!

## Nitroimidazoles

| Metronidazole                                     |
|---------------------------------------------------|
| Anaerobes, Protozoa, and Microaerophilic Bacteria |
| Gram-Negative/Atypicals                           |
| Bacteroides sp. Clostridium spp.                  |
| T. vaginalis                                      |
| Giardia lamblia                                   |
| G. vaginalis                                      |
| H. pylori (not monotherapy)                       |

Common indications: bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, diverticulitis

## Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile)

| First-Line (Oral)                            |
|----------------------------------------------|
| Vancomycin (Glycopeptide/Lipopetides)        |
| Fidaxomicin (Dificid) (Macrolide antibiotic) |
| Alternative                                  |
| Metronidazole                                |
